title: How did student midwife Success Eduan win European athletics gold?

evidence_packet.title: How did student midwife Success Eduan win European athletics gold?
evidence_packet.lead: Success Eduan balanced studying for her three-year midwife degree with her training as an elite athlete
evidence_packet.summary: Success Eduan balanced studying for her three-year midwife degree with her training as an elite athlete
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Getting to the top in any sport involves not only talent but also huge dedication and personal sacrifice Something the aptly named Success Eduan knows all about After reaching the individual 200m final at the recent European Championships in Birmingham, the 21-year-old athlete from Manchester won gold in the women's 4x100m relay Unknown to many, though, Eduan combined her gruelling training regime with completing a three-year degree in midwifery "It took a lot of grit, a lot of determination," the sprinter told BBC North West "There [were] times where I've not been able to fully train, just because mentally I'm exhausted from night shifts or from exams and things like that."

title: The Stockport shed cleaner who was awarded Victoria Cross

evidence_packet.title: The Stockport shed cleaner who was awarded Victoria Cross
evidence_packet.lead: Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner when World War One broke out in 1914
evidence_packet.summary: Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner when World War One broke out in 1914
evidence_packet.evidence_text: When World War One broke out in 1914, Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner But by the end of 1916, he had enlisted in the Cheshire Regiment of the British Army where he trained as a stretcher bearer to collect the wounded from the battlefields He was then transferred to the 10th Battalion Northumberland Fusiliers where he would later take part in one of the last battles of the World War One involving British soldiers fighting in Italy The Battle of Vittorio Veneto was fought from 24 October to 3 November 1918 and was seen as a decisive victory that contributed to the end of the war Mark Smith, who is a medals specialist at Stanley Gibbons Baldwins, said Wood went above and beyond what was expected of him and used his own initiative when his unit was held up by hostile machine guns and snipers The Stockport shed cleaner given the Victoria Cross

Additional Driver, featuring fellow indie artist Declan McKenna, was born from a minor car collision involving frontman Tom Ogden outside Manchester's O2 Apollo. The song tells the story of a journey from Manchester to Stockport that goes wrong, with the repeated refrain: "Should've got the 192". Image source, Ewan Ogden Image caption, The song's music video is shot on the 192 bus - one of the region's best-known routes. "Last year we went writing in Wales and invited Declan," Ogden explains. "I brought up a small bump I had in the car outside the Apollo, the previous week before the session. "A vocal take in the hot tub later we had finished writing what would become 'Additional Driver'. "We knew we wanted to try it out for the album so we invited Declan to Tilehouse when we were recording the album." Image source, Ewan Ogden Image caption, Blossoms have had four number one albums in the UK charts Blossoms are following in the footsteps of other successful indie and rock bands who have found inspiration on Britain's buses. The Clash referenced London's No. 19 bus in Rudie Can't Fail, while Birmingham band Superfood featured the No. 9 route in Unstoppable. title: How will Manchester Pride be different this year?

evidence_packet.title: How will Manchester Pride be different this year?
evidence_packet.lead: A new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC) has taken over running of the four-day event
evidence_packet.summary: A new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC) has taken over running of the four-day event
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The August bank holiday weekend has been home to Manchester Pride for more than 40 years From its humble beginnings in 1985 as a fundraiser for Monsall Hospital's HIV and Aids ward, Manchester Pride grew into one of the country's biggest LGBTQ+ events When the company behind it went into voluntary liquidation last year, many were worried there would be no Pride in 2026 But Manchester City Council tried to allay fears when, in January, it announced that a new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC), Manchester Village Pride, would take over the running of the four-day event Manchester Village Pride is run by volunteer directors and is mainly made up of businesses from Manchester's Gay Village Venues in the area have loaned the new organisation £120,000 to support the planning and delivery of the event

evidence_packet.lead: Manchester Airport is expecting around half a million passengers this bank holiday
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester Airport is expecting around half a million passengers this bank holiday
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport warns passengers ahead of busy bank holiday - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, Passengers are being warned not to pack items powered by lithium batteries in hold bags By Haider Saleem Reporting from North West Published 28 August 2026 Passengers travelling through Manchester Airport over the August bank holiday weekend have been warned to check how they pack to help reduce delays during one of the busiest weekends in the airport's history. The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) has urged travellers to avoid packing battery-powered devices in hold luggage as they pose a fire risk. It said bags may have to be offloaded if items such as vapes and power banks are found in them. About two million passengers are expected to depart from airports across Great Britain during the weekend, according to the regulator. 'Catch fire without warning' Anthony Shaw, a security team leader in the airport's hold baggage screening team, said staff often find devices including vapes, power banks and tablets in checked luggage. "If the battery gets too hot, or is faulty, it can catch fire without warning," he said. Shaw said staff could screen almost 1,000 bags for a large long-haul aircraft and several hundred for a short-haul flight. "Each bag that fails to pass security checks gets pulled aside, and often needs to be inspected manually," he said. "This can create delays, but it also creates a risk that your hold bag might not make it onto the plane at all." The CAA said a fire on board could result in an aircraft being diverted or evacuated. Vapes, power banks and spare batteries must be carried in the cabin rather than placed in checked baggage. title: Bolton Food and Drink Festival to attract 500,000 visitors

evidence_packet.title: Bolton Food and Drink Festival to attract 500,000 visitors
evidence_packet.lead: Top chefs, live bands and free samples are promised for the four day event
evidence_packet.summary: Top chefs, live bands and free samples are promised for the four day event
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Food and Drink Festival to attract 500,000 visitors - BBC News Image source, Bolton Council Image caption, The festival began in 2005 and is the biggest food and drink festival in England By Paul Burnell North West Published 28 August 2026 More than half a million people are expected to attend Bolton's Food and Drink Festival as over 100 food vendors will serve up tasty meals and drinks over four days. Big name chefs include James Martin, Marco Pierre White and Nisha Katona will serve up cooking demos. The festival site is spread across the town centre and organisers suggest Victoria Square information point is the best place for visitors to collect a free guide to help plan their day. Debbie Newall, Bolton Council's executive cabinet member for culture, said: "This is an opportunity to support local traders, celebrate fantastic food and drink, and showcase the very best of Bolton." "From artisan stalls and celebrity chef demonstrations, to live music and family activities, there is something for everyone to enjoy. "We are so proud of the continued success of the festival, and I urge everyone to visit and show their support." Free events taking place include street performers, children's activities, live music and entertainment throughout the weekend including headliners Liberty X and The Real Thing with demonstrations from regional chefs at Victoria Square. Meanwhile interactive experiences across the festival site include circus skills workshops, giant doodle walls, bubble performances, creative art sessions and a giant sandpit. title: Salford to extend long-term home-building plans

evidence_packet.title: Salford to extend long-term home-building plans
evidence_packet.lead: Salford City Council sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043
evidence_packet.summary: Salford City Council sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford to extend long-term home-building plans - BBC News Image caption, Mike McCusker is the council's lead member for planning By Richard Stead North West Published 28 August 2026 Members of the public are being invited to have their say about plans to build nearly 35,000 new homes in Salford over the next 17 years - while also protecting the city's greenery. Extending the council's home-building plans by four years, a new document has sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043. Deputy mayor and planning boss Mike McCusker said: "We will have a brand new development plan, which will give us a good pipeline of new homes as well as protection from developers, who could successfully appeal against planning applications which the council has rejected. "At the same time its important to protect our valuable green spaces for local people." Salford Council's existing local plan, which is part of the Greater Manchester-wide Places For Everyone strategy, outlines sites to be developed until 2039. Image caption, The draft local plan outlines the ambition to build warehouses on empty land next to the Salford Community Stadium The city has been one of the fastest growing in the UK over recent years, with its population rising to 294,000 in 2024 - an increase of 34% since 2001. Most of that growth has been in the city centre - and at Salford Quays - but there have also been new homes built on former green belt land in areas like Boothstown. Councillors will vote on the draft local plan before the end of this year and it will then be submitted to the government for final approval. evidence_packet.evidence_text: When World War One broke out in 1914, Wilfred Wood was working on the railways as a shed cleaner But by the end of 1916, he had enlisted in the Cheshire Regiment of the British Army where he trained as a stretcher bearer to collect the wounded from the battlefields He was then transferred to the 10th Battalion Northumberland Fusiliers where he would later take part in one of the last battles of the World War One involving British soldiers fighting in Italy The Battle of Vittorio Veneto was fought from 24 October to 3 November 1918 and was seen as a decisive victory that contributed to the end of the war Mark Smith, who is a medals specialist at Stanley Gibbons Baldwins, said Wood went above and beyond what was expected of him and used his own initiative when his unit was held up by hostile machine guns and snipers The Stockport shed cleaner given the Victoria Cross

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The August bank holiday weekend has been home to Manchester Pride for more than 40 years From its humble beginnings in 1985 as a fundraiser for Monsall Hospital's HIV and Aids ward, Manchester Pride grew into one of the country's biggest LGBTQ+ events When the company behind it went into voluntary liquidation last year, many were worried there would be no Pride in 2026 But Manchester City Council tried to allay fears when, in January, it announced that a new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC), Manchester Village Pride, would take over the running of the four-day event Manchester Village Pride is run by volunteer directors and is mainly made up of businesses from Manchester's Gay Village Venues in the area have loaned the new organisation £120,000 to support the planning and delivery of the event

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport council accused of U-turn after plan to increase bin collections Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 07:42, 29 Aug 2026 View Ima Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ following a major bin announcement. But top councillors said there would be no cuts to services as a result of the change From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport . The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025 Earlier this week, councillor Jake Austin, who is the cabinet member overseeing bin services, said he was delighted to announce the move and feedback had been ‘loud and clear’ that people ‘want a service that makes it easier to recycle’ Council leader Mark Roberts said: “It is critical people know the Liberal Democrats will listen to the feedback given and strive to make a positive difference wherever we can.” The announcement this week has come after weeks of criticism of the local authority . Recent controversial enforcement of a long-standing policy around collecting bins with open lids led to hundreds of people being left with uncollected bins

evidence_packet.summary: Bolton The tragedy they knew was coming Four men were killed in a horrific head-on crash - but on the road where it happened, residents expect another major incident View 9 Images Mohammed Jibrael Mukhtar, Mohammed-Danyaal Asghar-Ali, Farhan Patel and News Stephen Topping Senior
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton The tragedy they knew was coming Four men were killed in a horrific head-on crash - but on the road where it happened, residents expect another major incident View 9 Images Mohammed Jibrael Mukhtar, Mohammed-Danyaal Asghar-Ali, Farhan Patel and News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:00, 29 Aug 2026 Updated 07:18, 29 Aug 2026 It was the scene of a devastating tragedy. Four lives lost in a moment. Countless others torn apart Three teenagers and a dad-of-four taxi driver died following a head-on crash on Wigan Road, in Bolton , at 12.45am on Sunday, January 11. Hundreds of people have been left to grieve for their loved ones Those who survived the crash have had to come to terms with horrific injuries . But in the community where those harrowing scenes unfolded, there is a sense that drivers are still refusing to take the risks of the road seriously "I do think it shocked a few people, but it won’t be long before there’s another one," Melissa McCarney said. The 19-year-old was one of a string of residents living close to the crash scene who spoke to the Manchester Evening News this week More than seven months on from the crash, road safety is still a constant source of concern for residents. Neighbours describe having had multiple cars written off over the years, on a street likened to a 'race track'

evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Police Police descend on Toby Carvery in Chadderton Park as 'man tasered in car park' The restaurant based in Chadderton Park was closed on Friday evening (August 28) Comments News Charlotte Fisher and Amy Walker Court reporter 22:1 Emergency services descended
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Police descend on Toby Carvery in Chadderton Park as 'man tasered in car park' The restaurant based in Chadderton Park was closed on Friday evening (August 28) Comments News Charlotte Fisher and Amy Walker Court reporter 22:1 Emergency services descended on a Toby Carvery restaurant after reports a man was 'tasered' by police this evening, Friday, August 28 The restaurant, located on Chadderton Park, Oldham , was closed for a short period of time after a number of police cars and an ambulance were spotted outside, witnesses said Pictures from the scene show a police car remained at the scene after the restaurant reopened around an hour later The Manchester Evening News that a man appeared to have been running from police officers before he was tasered in the car park. title: EasyJet nightmare as pilot cancels Manchester Airport flight on the runway before replacement ends up 1,290 miles from destination

evidence_packet.title: EasyJet nightmare as pilot cancels Manchester Airport flight on the runway before replacement ends up 1,290 miles from destination
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester Airport EasyJet nightmare as pilot cancels Manchester Airport flight on the runway before replacement ends up 1,290 miles from destination Passengers have been left 'stranded' after a pilot at Manchester Airport suddenly cancelled their fli Hundreds of holiday-goers ha
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester Airport EasyJet nightmare as pilot cancels Manchester Airport flight on the runway before replacement ends up 1,290 miles from destination Passengers have been left 'stranded' after a pilot at Manchester Airport suddenly cancelled their fli Hundreds of holiday-goers ha
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport EasyJet nightmare as pilot cancels Manchester Airport flight on the runway before replacement ends up 1,290 miles from destination Passengers have been left 'stranded' after a pilot at Manchester Airport suddenly cancelled their fli Hundreds of holiday-goers have been left hit by hours of delays and stuck 1,200 miles from their destination after their flight from Manchester was suddenly cancelled Passengers on the easyJet flight to Antalya this morning, Friday (August 28), say they were told to leave the runway 'ten minutes' before their flight was due to depart. One passenger said they were due to board the plane when they were told to return to the terminal. The airline But following a wait of more than four hours, passengers, who were originally due to depart at 7.45am, eventually took off to their holiday destination at around 12pm after a replacement crew was found, the Manchester Evening News understands However, when in the air, passengers say they were told the flight needed to divert to Milan, as the staff couldn't legally carry on working as the crew had reached its duty-time limit Passengers from the plane, which they said largely consisted of families with young children, were taken to Milan Airport - over 1,200 miles from their destination. They have been given a €25 food voucher while they wait for their new crew to arrive, apparently coming from Manche

The hearing was told he was on his way to an emergen The hearing was told the van left the scene without stopping. The owner of the Seat reported the collision to GMP and it was captured on Ring doorbell footage

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Man, 28, sexually assaulted girl after asking her what 'favours' she would do for him in return for a vape Furqan Khalil assaulted the victim at his mobile phone and e-cigarette shop News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 14:54, 28 Aug 2026 View Image A 28-year-old man from Bolton has been found guilty of sexually assaulting a girl in Northwich. After she chose a vape, Khalil told her to wait outside, claiming he could not give it to her inside because of the CCTV cameras Once outside, Khalil again touched the victim inappropriately. When she asked for the vape, he instead asked what “favours” she would do for him in return

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Cowboy builder overpromised, underdelivered and left families 'in a state' He caused £1m of damage - but now he is behind bars News Rachel Smith Court reporter and Stephen Topping Senior reporter 14:12, 28 Aug 2026 View Image Patrick Hartley A cowboy builder who 'overpromised and underdelivered' left damage worth £1m to homes in Greater Manchester and Lancashire . A court heard how Patrick Hartley left homeowners without adequate roofing The 40-year-old would take customers' money before moving on to the next job, leaving work unfinished. His actions put families under strain as they took on more debt to have the work put right, Lancs Live reports The court heard Hartley, from Bacup, Rossendale, stung 13 families in a 30-month period from 2020. His fraudulent activity landed him a prison sentence of three years and nine months Judge Andrew Jeffries KC told him: "Any conscientious builder would simply have stopped. The court heard Hartley was sent written letters and warnings after customers complained about the work. In some cases the builder promised refunds which never came

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Parklife Festival Seven people arrested in London raids linked to string of Parklife Festival robberies Police say some of the victims were attacked News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 10:55, 28 Aug 2026 Updated 12:09, 28 Aug 2026 Greater Manchester Victims reported being approached in crowded areas of the festival and asked to hand over valuable items, including mobile phones and jewellery. GMP says that in several incidents, those who resisted - or those who had friends that stepped in to help - were subjected to violence Investigators believe members of the group would walk through the crowds and pass the stolen items back and forth, making it difficult to track where they had gone. CCTV footage allowed victims to identify one suspect While being arrested on suspicion of robbery, investigators seized and examined his mobile phone. GMP says officers discovered evidence which indicated a wider criminal network had been in operation Further evidence and intelligence led to a joint operation between GMP and Metropolitan Police, who executed warrants at 12 addresses across London on Wednesday morning (August 26). Seven people were arrested on suspicion of robbery and other related offences View Image It follows a string of incidents at this year's Parklife Festival (Image: Manchester Evening News)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tameside Pensioner fighting for life being hit by Toyota Yaris in Ashton-under-Lyne Witnesses are being urged to come forward News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 08:09, 28 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Police at the scene yesterday (Image: ASP) A man in his 70s is fighting for his life after being hit by a car in Tameside . Emergency services descended on Huddersfield Road , in Ashton-under-Lyne , on Thursday afternoon (August 27) Greater Manchester Police says it was called out to a collision at around 2.40pm. It's believed a Toyota Yaris was turning off Huddersfield Road when it hit the pedestrian He was rushed to hospital for treatment, where he remains in a life-threatening conditions this morning (Friday). GMP says the driver remained at the scene of the crash No arrests have been made following the incident. Part of Huddersfield Road remained closed for hours following the incident, while an air ambulance was pictured landing nearby North West Ambulance Service said it 'dispatched several ambulance resources to the scene' including the air ambulance. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport council accused of U-turn after plan to increase bin collections Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 07:42, 29 Aug 2026 View Ima Stockport council’s leadership has been accused of ‘making policy on the back of a fag packet’ following a major bin announcement. But top councillors said there would be no cuts to services as a result of the change From the beginning of December 2026, blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling will be collected every two weeks instead of every four weeks across Stockport . The council moved to four weekly collections due to financial pressures on its budget for day-to-day services in 2025 Earlier this week, councillor Jake Austin, who is the cabinet member overseeing bin services, said he was delighted to announce the move and feedback had been ‘loud and clear’ that people ‘want a service that makes it easier to recycle’ Council leader Mark Roberts said: “It is critical people know the Liberal Democrats will listen to the feedback given and strive to make a positive difference wherever we can.” The announcement this week has come after weeks of criticism of the local authority . Recent controversial enforcement of a long-standing policy around collecting bins with open lids led to hundreds of people being left with uncollected bins

evidence_packet.evidence_text: By Hannah Richardson 07:22, 29 AUG 2026 Bookmark The new Radcliffe Hub is expected to open this autumn (Image: Christian Smith / Bury council) Promised to be the ‘heart of a thriving, active Radcliffe ’ the town’s new hub has taken another ‘significant step fo The building, in Dale Street, will boast a library, swimming pool and 100-station gym. There will also be a climbing wall, café, rooftop activity space and dedicated children’s area This week, the keys to the building were handed over to Bury council, with the authority saying this marks a ‘major milestone’. The contractors have finished their part in the £40m project, with the council now set to get the ‘final fixtures and fittings’ in place The hub is ‘on track’ to open this autumn, leaders have said. Prices and opening hours are expected to be in line with other leisure centres in the borough Now, new pictures and video show the inside of the building and the community spaces that are coming together Lead member for adult care, health and public service reform Tamoor Tariq said: “This is really going to be at the beating heart of the Radcliffe community, but a leisure facility for the whole borough. title: The tragedy they knew was coming

evidence_packet.title: The tragedy they knew was coming
evidence_packet.lead: Bolton The tragedy they knew was coming Four men were killed in a horrific head-on crash - but on the road where it happened, residents expect another major incident View 9 Images Mohammed Jibrael Mukhtar, Mohammed-Danyaal Asghar-Ali, Farhan Patel and News Stephen Topping Senior
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton The tragedy they knew was coming Four men were killed in a horrific head-on crash - but on the road where it happened, residents expect another major incident View 9 Images Mohammed Jibrael Mukhtar, Mohammed-Danyaal Asghar-Ali, Farhan Patel and News Stephen Topping Senior
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton The tragedy they knew was coming Four men were killed in a horrific head-on crash - but on the road where it happened, residents expect another major incident View 9 Images Mohammed Jibrael Mukhtar, Mohammed-Danyaal Asghar-Ali, Farhan Patel and News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:00, 29 Aug 2026 Updated 07:18, 29 Aug 2026 It was the scene of a devastating tragedy. Four lives lost in a moment. Countless others torn apart Three teenagers and a dad-of-four taxi driver died following a head-on crash on Wigan Road, in Bolton , at 12.45am on Sunday, January 11. Hundreds of people have been left to grieve for their loved ones Those who survived the crash have had to come to terms with horrific injuries . But in the community where those harrowing scenes unfolded, there is a sense that drivers are still refusing to take the risks of the road seriously "I do think it shocked a few people, but it won’t be long before there’s another one," Melissa McCarney said. The 19-year-old was one of a string of residents living close to the crash scene who spoke to the Manchester Evening News this week More than seven months on from the crash, road safety is still a constant source of concern for residents. Neighbours describe having had multiple cars written off over the years, on a street likened to a 'race track'

evidence_packet.summary: Bury The full story of the flashy young drug dealer shot by police as his empire crumbled Officers have now been told they are not under investigation for their conduct View 6 Images Lewis Hanson (Image: GMP) News Paul Britton Reporter 06:00, 29 Aug 2026 Boxed in by police firear
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury The full story of the flashy young drug dealer shot by police as his empire crumbled Officers have now been told they are not under investigation for their conduct View 6 Images Lewis Hanson (Image: GMP) News Paul Britton Reporter 06:00, 29 Aug 2026 Boxed in by police firearms officers in his trendy Cupra car, years of drug dealing on the streets came to a dramatic end for Lewis Hanson. Unbeknown to him, the flashy criminal Hanson had been under surveillance Cops from GMP's Serious and Organised Crime Group watched as he visited a drugs stash house in Radcliffe, Bury, and drove around Radcliffe, Whitefield and Greenmount They saw him make street deals with users - then made their move just after 3pm on May 22, at the junction of Bury New Road and Chestnut Avenue in Whitefield. Hanson, 20, who spent thousands on designer clothes, 'attempted to evade arrest', Greater Manchester Police said this wee The officers involved in what became a firearms operation attempted to stop the Cupra, but the force said Hanson failed to comply and 'attempted to evade capture' In turn, officers discharged a single shot, striking him in the elbow. A sentencing hearing in court was told one of the attending armed officers 'felt compelled to discharge his firearm'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre Man City star's £200k Mercedes 'clamped on Manchester back street as he got haircut' Forward Omar Marmoush found his car clamped after parking in a 'loading only' bay Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer and Jam Press 08 A parking howler has reportedly resulted in a Manchester City star's £200,000 car being clamped. 27-year-old star Omar Marmoush was caught out by the council, which left the Egyptian ace with a lock on his wheel and a ticket on his windshield The winger, who signed for City in January 2025 for £59m, had parked his 2025 Mercedes-Benz AMG G 63 MHEV down a back street in the city centre while he got a haircut, according to reports A swish £200,000 motor was spotted with the clamp on South King Street , Manchester The vehicle was spotted in a ‘loading only’ bay on Aug 14 around 8.30 pm. Manchester City Council’s removal fee for a clamp can reach up to £105 if the owner fails to contact them within 24 hours The car will then be towed to the pound where the owner will be charged £12 a day until the vehicle is collected. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Heartless Bacup builder showed 13 families 'no mercy' as he pocketed £700,000 and left a trail of devastation The cowboy builder 'showed no mercy' to families across Greater Manchester and Lancashire Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 16:09, 2 The conviction of a cowboy builder has been welcomed by council investigators who described him as 'one of the most prolific, heartless fraudsters that we have come across' Patrick Hartley, 40, 'overpromised and underdelivered' - and left damage worth £1m to homes in Greater Manchester and Lancashire , a court heard Hartley would take customers' money before moving on to the next job, leaving work unfinished and families under strain as they took on more debt to have the work put right Council bosses said he targeted homes in Oldham , Tameside , Sale , Bury , Bolton and Stockport , as well as in Bacup and Rawtenstall. One of his victims included a couple in Bacup, who asked Hartley to build an extension for an elderly relative so they could take her in during h After Hartley was jailed on Friday, Lancashire County Council issued a statement, saying he preyed on people when they were vulnerable for financial gain

It was lovely to see, but we were just being ourselves at the same time - we weren’t pretending to be something else.” When Cleopatra first emerged onto the pop scene with the release of their debut single Cleopatra’s Theme in 1998, there was nobody else like them. And within weeks of their first single reaching the top five in the charts, Yonah, Cleopatra and Zainam - aged just 15, 17 and 18 at Cleopatra became a global sensation, signing to Madonna’s label, Maverick, in the United States and touring the world. “It got us out of Moss Side and out of the country,” says Cleo, who has been speaking with Yonah to our LGBT+ Writer Adam Maidment View 7 Images Yonah and Cleo from Cleopatra (Image: Cleopatra) “We were literally famous. It was overwhelming - it all went very quickly for us,” Cleo says This weekend, the girls will perform at Manchester Pride. But before that, they spent some time chatting to Adam about their 90s pop stardom and their current shows as Cleopatra and as solo artists

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Royal Manchester Children's Hospital Some kids are left with a twisted ankle, some serious brain injuries. Some end up dead Children as young as seven are being seriously injured on e-scooters. New research reveals a dramatic rise in youngsters ending News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 14:34, 28 Aug 2026 Updated 15:18, 28 Aug 2026 Doctors treating injured children say there is a dangerous misconception amid the growing popularity of e-scooters Medics in Greater Manchester say they are seeing "several" e-scooter incidents every week. Youngsters have been left with with devastating brain injuries. Sew research reveals the scale of the problem hitting hospitals "We obviously see a lot of minor injuries, which are ankle injuries and upper limb injuries," Caroline Rushmer, children's major trauma coordinator at Royal Manchester Children's Hospital told the Manchester Evening News "But we're also seeing really significant injuries. In some cases, life-altering injuries as a result of using e-scooters." Caroline recalled the case of one boy who crashed after hitting a pothole hidden beneath fallen leaves. Another child, aged just seven, suffered a serious leg break after twisting the throttle on a friend's e-scooter without realising what it did

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Man, 28, sexually assaulted girl after asking her what 'favours' she would do for him in return for a vape Furqan Khalil assaulted the victim at his mobile phone and e-cigarette shop News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 14:54, 28 Aug 2026 View Image A 28-year-old man from Bolton has been found guilty of sexually assaulting a girl in Northwich. Furqan Khalil assaulted the girl at his mobile phone and e-cigarette shop, asking her what “favours” she would do for him in return for a vape Khalil of Rishton Lane, Bolton , was found guilty of engaging in non-penetrative sexual activity with a child following a four-day trial at Chester Crown Court which concluded on Thursday (August 27) The court heard that in February 2024, the victim entered Khalil’s mobile phone and e-cigarette shop in Northwich to buy a phone charger While in the shop, she asked whether she could purchase a vape. As Khalil showed her a selection, he touched her inappropriately. After she chose a vape, Khalil told her to wait outside, claiming he could not give it to her inside because of the CCTV cameras Once outside, Khalil again touched the victim inappropriately. When she asked for the vape, he instead asked what “favours” she would do for him in return

evidence_packet.lead: Courts Cowboy builder overpromised, underdelivered and left families 'in a state' He caused £1m of damage - but now he is behind bars News Rachel Smith Court reporter and Stephen Topping Senior reporter 14:12, 28 Aug 2026 View Image Patrick Hartley A cowboy builder who 'overpromi
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Cowboy builder overpromised, underdelivered and left families 'in a state' He caused £1m of damage - but now he is behind bars News Rachel Smith Court reporter and Stephen Topping Senior reporter 14:12, 28 Aug 2026 View Image Patrick Hartley A cowboy builder who 'overpromi
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Cowboy builder overpromised, underdelivered and left families 'in a state' He caused £1m of damage - but now he is behind bars News Rachel Smith Court reporter and Stephen Topping Senior reporter 14:12, 28 Aug 2026 View Image Patrick Hartley A cowboy builder who 'overpromised and underdelivered' left damage worth £1m to homes in Greater Manchester and Lancashire . A court heard how Patrick Hartley left homeowners without adequate roofing The 40-year-old would take customers' money before moving on to the next job, leaving work unfinished. His actions put families under strain as they took on more debt to have the work put right, Lancs Live reports The court heard Hartley, from Bacup, Rossendale, stung 13 families in a 30-month period from 2020. His fraudulent activity landed him a prison sentence of three years and nine months Judge Andrew Jeffries KC told him: "Any conscientious builder would simply have stopped. You continued to take on fresh work when the truth was you were leaving jobs incomplete and families in a state." The court heard Hartley was sent written letters and warnings after customers complained about the work. In some cases the builder promised refunds which never came

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Parklife Festival Seven people arrested in London raids linked to string of Parklife Festival robberies Police say some of the victims were attacked News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 10:55, 28 Aug 2026 Updated 12:09, 28 Aug 2026 Greater Manchester Victims reported being approached in crowded areas of the festival and asked to hand over valuable items, including mobile phones and jewellery. GMP says that in several incidents, those who resisted - or those who had friends that stepped in to help - were subjected to violence Investigators believe members of the group would walk through the crowds and pass the stolen items back and forth, making it difficult to track where they had gone. CCTV footage allowed victims to identify one suspect While being arrested on suspicion of robbery, investigators seized and examined his mobile phone. GMP says officers discovered evidence which indicated a wider criminal network had been in operation Further evidence and intelligence led to a joint operation between GMP and Metropolitan Police, who executed warrants at 12 addresses across London on Wednesday morning (August 26). Seven people were arrested on suspicion of robbery and other related offences View Image It follows a string of incidents at this year's Parklife Festival (Image: Manchester Evening News)

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Marc Powell, from Whaley Bridge, Derbyshire, has the SOD1 variant of the disease, which affects fewer than 100 people in the UK Drug manufacturer Biogen is supplying Tofersen free of charge to specialist centres, including Salford Royal, while the NHS decides whether to fund it However, hospitals must cover the costs of administering it, so numbers are limited. The Northern Care Alliance NHS Trust said Tofersen was not currently commissioned by NHS England and required specialist expertise and support to deliver safely Marc, who celebrated his 60th birthday this week, was diagnosed with MND in January after noticing problems with his speech "I got home and sobbed my heart out with my wife," he said "I thought 'That's it - life plan out of the window, not much time left.'

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Nights you don't want to miss - Opening NightCome and join us for our first performance.Buy tickets Go behind the music and inside the story of Frankie Valli and The Four Seasons in the true-life musical phenomenon, Jersey Boys. From the streets of New Jersey to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, this is the musical that’s too good to be true. They were just four guys from Jersey, until they sang their very first note. They had a sound nobody had ever heard… and the radio just couldn’t get enough of. But while their harmonies were perfect on stage, off stage it was a very different story -- a story that has made them an international sensation all over again. The show features all their hits including “Sherry,” “Big Girls Don’t Cry,” “Walk Like A Man,” “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You,” “Beggin’,” “December 1963 (Oh What a Night)” and more. The 20th Anniversary tour boasts a stellar cast, lead by Luke Baker (Everybody’s Talking About Jamie, Sheffield/West End; Billy Elliot, Curve Leicester) as Frankie Valli, Carlo Boumouglbay (Muriel’s Wedding, Curve Leicester; Miss Saigon, international tour) as Tommy Devito, Lewis Kennedy (All male Pirates of Penzance, Wilton’s Music Hall) as Nick Massi, Toby Miles (Les Misérables, West End; School of Rock, international tour) as Bob Gaudio and Ellis Kirk (Dear Evan Hansen, West End/Asia tour) as Alternate Frankie Valli. Please note: The following performances are Access Performances - Thursday 10th September 2026 – 19:30: Audio Described Tuesday 15th September 2026 – 19:30: Captioned Buy direct from venues with ATG Tickets. I’m not encouraging that in a million years. I don’t know if it would be too tight for time. Deals and contracts are taking much longer now. There seems to be a lot more involved.” Everton remain interested in City’s Jack Grealish, who spent last season on loan at Hill Dickinson Stadium, but a right-back and centre-forward are more of a priority. Its approach is rooted in tradition but interpreted through a contemporary lens – cr At the heart of Coco Tang is a belief that Vietnamese hospitality extends far beyond food, with the experience beginning with the first coffee of the day and continuing through to the final cocktail of the night. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
